provenance: The audit-2 auditor (Opus, independent) was interrupted when the host session ended, before it wrote this file. The Orchestrator compiled this file on 2026-09-27 from the auditor's raw evidence in this directory, without re-running or re-interpreting anything. Items the auditor never reached are listed under notReached.

findings.title: GAP-220 residual is real and common: a blank popup (window.open('') / about:blank) that alerts synchronously, or via document.write inline script, is missed entirely
findings.repro: w = window.open(''); w.alert(...) | w.confirm | w.prompt | w.document.write('<script>alert()</script>') | a CLI click that opens such a popup
findings.rate: 26/26 MISS (warden list empty, `dialog` says no dialog; next snap hangs 180 s then exits 0 on about:blank, or hits the 30 s probe cap). An independently attached raw CDP session DID see the dialog in every case (rawSaw) -- so it is observable, the warden just does not observe it.

findings.title: After the gate applies a policy (--dialog accept|dismiss) to one dialog, a follow-up dialog (alert -> confirm chain) is not re-gated: the command runs anyway, hangs 180 s, and returns exit 0 from the wrong tab (about:blank)
findings.repro: popup alerts then confirms; run `snap --dialog accept` / `snap --dialog dismiss` / `eval 1 --dialog accept`
findings.rate: 4/4 variants x trials observed (180.4 s, exit 0, URL about:blank, stillBlocked true). Control `dialog accept` handles it correctly in 480 ms.

findings.title: An `unknown` dialog is a dead end: `dialog accept|dismiss` and `--dialog accept` all fail "No dialog is open on that tab", `tabs` is gated (exit 3) so the tab id needed by `closetab` cannot be learned, and only `close` (losing the whole session) escapes
findings.repro: any case that yields type unknown (e.g., window.open + inline alert), then dialog accept / dialog dismiss / snap --dialog accept / tabs / closetab
findings.rate: 3/3 trials, every recovery command except close

findings.title: GAP-223 spawn lock is not reliable: with a stale lock present, concurrent commands still spawn multiple wardens and the stale lock can be left behind; plain concurrency also occasionally spawns 2; double-handling reproduces
findings.repro: lock-race-probe (stale / plain / crash variants); r10 probe with a stale lock and no warden.json
findings.rate: stale: 8/10 rounds multi-warden (max 4), lock left 1/10; plain: 1/10 rounds 2 wardens; r10 stale-nojson: 1/4 runs had 2 wardens and 3/10 chains resolved the prompt with '' instead of the default. Unmodified r10 probe: 1 warden, 10/10 (holds).

findings.title: Surviving mutations: dialog-id targeting (the GAP-223 identity half) is untested; the warden never releasing its own paused attach is untested; the liveness-probe time budget is untested
findings.repro: mutations.mjs M9, M10, M10b, M16, M17
findings.rate: 5 of 20 mutations survive; the other 15 (WD7, WD3, DirectCdpBroker unknown, WC5, WC6, S-D1/S-D2, GAP-221, GAP-220 WD9/11/12, GAP-222, gate dispose) are killed

findings.title: beforeunload in a popup is neither detected nor blocking (warden reports no dialog, snap returns normally)
findings.rate: 2/2; possibly correct by design (beforeunload only fires on navigation) -- the auditor marked it "no test", needs a fixture that actually triggers it

signalResearch.question: 2(c): is there a decidable signal separating "dialog open" from "busy script"?
signalResearch.answer: Yes, promising, not yet productised: Performance.getMetrics and Debugger.setBreakpointsActive ANSWER under a busy synchronous script (4/4 trials each) but TIME OUT under an open alert/confirm/prompt/beforeunload (4/4 each). Runtime.evaluate, Page.getFrameTree and Runtime.getIsolateId time out in BOTH states (not decidable) -- which is exactly why fix-1 false-blocked N9/N10 when it probed with Runtime.evaluate. Page.getNavigationHistory answered even under beforeunload.
